terms.definition: A new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or an improvement thereof. Laws of nature, natural phenomena, and abstract ideas are judicial exceptions.
The invention must have a specific, substantial, and credible utility (35 U.S.C. 101).
A claim is anticipated, and unpatentable, if a single prior art reference discloses every element of it, expressly or inherently.

A claim is unpatentable if the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date. Graham v. John Deere sets the factual inquiries.
Scope and content of the prior art; differences between the prior art and the claims; level of ordinary skill in the art; and objective indicia of nonobviousness (secondary considerations).
The specification must describe the invention, and enable a person skilled in the art to make and use it, and set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor.
The claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter the inventor regards as the invention.
A cheap, never-examined application that secures a filing date; it lapses after 12 months unless a non-provisional claiming its benefit is filed.
The standard application that is examined; it requires a specification, at least one claim, drawings where necessary, and an oath or declaration.
Title, cross-references, background, summary, brief description of drawings, detailed description, claims, and abstract.
An independent claim stands on its own; a dependent claim refers to and further limits an earlier claim.
20 years from the earliest effective non-provisional filing date, subject to patent term adjustment and maintenance fees.
15 years from grant for applications filed on or after May 13, 2015.
A filing that, with a fee, reopens prosecution after a final rejection so new arguments or amendments can be considered.
A non-final action is the first or later rejection allowing full response with new amendments; a final action closes prosecution, limiting further amendments as of right.

terms.term: Response period to an Office action
terms.definition: Usually a 3-month shortened statutory period, extendable by fee to a maximum of 6 months.
A submission in which applicants disclose known material prior art, in satisfaction of the duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56.
The examiner's requirement that an application be limited to one of several independent or distinct inventions.
A new application claiming the same disclosure as a parent, filed while the parent is pending, with the same inventors in common; it gets the parent's filing date.
A new application that repeats part of a parent's disclosure and adds new matter; only the shared subject matter gets the parent's date.
An application filed for an invention that was restricted out of a parent application.
An applicant may claim priority to an earlier first filing in a member country if the later application is filed within 12 months (6 months for designs).
A treaty providing a single international application, with national phase entry generally at 30 months from the priority date.

terms.term: Pre-AIA vs. AIA first inventor to file
terms.definition: Applications with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013 follow first-inventor-to-file rules; earlier ones follow first-to-invent.
A disclosure by the inventor made 1 year or less before the effective filing date is not prior art under the 102(b)(1) exceptions.
Due at 3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years after grant; each can be paid in a 6-month grace period with a surcharge.
A PTAB trial challenging patent claims as unpatentable under 102 or 103 based on patents and printed publications.
Each individual associated with filing and prosecuting an application must disclose information material to patentability.
35 U.S.C. (statute), 37 C.F.R. (rules), and the MPEP (the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure, the examiners' and practitioners' guide).
